ONE MECHANISM ACROSS THIS BATCH (rule 3), recorded at every site: the sim's monster ports drop PowerCmd.Apply's `applier` argument. C# is `Apply<T>(choiceContext, target, amount, applier, cardSource)` (PowerCmd.cs:67) and passes `base.Creature` at SpinyToad.cs:82 and :92 (ThornsPower, applier=base.Creature); the sim's `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, target, power_cls, amount, applier=None)` (cmds.py:271-277) is called without it at spiny_toad.py:45 and :51. In C# a null applier additionally SKIPS the whole Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven pass (PowerCmd.cs:123-126) and changes the key FindExistingInstanceForStacking uses (PowerCmd.cs:78, :112). Same observable today, EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py applier`): the sim has exactly six listener definitions that can see the argument -- powers.py:1172/1181 (ViciousPower, gated `name != "vulnerable" or applier is not self.owner`, powers.py:1167), powers.py:3101/3106 (_PossessPower, gated `applier is self.owner and name == self._stat_id and target.side == "player" and delta < 0`, powers.py:3092-3099), relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 (gated on `target is self.player`, never on applier) and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (gated `applier is not self.player`, unsettling_lamp.py:47). None can distinguish `None` from the applying monster for a power this unit applies. Named trigger: porting any listener that reads `applier` positively (a monster-applier-sensitive relic), or porting PowerInstanceType so stacking is keyed by applier.
